summary: No-ship. F2, F4, F5, and F6 are substantively dispositioned and their runtime claims check out, but F1 remains contradicted by the opening scope statement, and B6 cannot reliably observe the incomplete-read condition it claims to count. All 43 explicit file:line citations resolve.

findings.title: F1 remains contradicted by the spec's opening product claim
findings.body: The spec still says each run writes a dream report and that a run skipping 191 sessions produces one. src/cli/dream.js:736-757 proves otherwise: zero-admission exclusion runs throw without promotion, while quarantine-only runs print "nothing new to dream" and return without a report. Table A later states this correctly, leaving two conflicting coverage contracts. This can preserve the exact misunderstanding F1 was supposed to remove without requiring any product-scope expansion.
findings.recommendation: Qualify both sentences to say that only a real, non-dry run admitting at least one session and reaching promote() composes the report; explicitly frame the 191-session example as a mixed run with at least one admission.

findings.title: The read-deferred count cannot reliably observe the condition it promises
findings.body: B6 claims to count transcripts whose read exceeded the per-session allowance. In production, scratch.js admits only discovery records at or below 50 MiB and gives each parser a fresh 200 MiB budget. An unchanged eligible file therefore cannot exhaust that budget. Worse, stream.js:129-136 decides whether unread bytes remain by comparing 200 MiB consumed against the stale discovery size. If a file grows from at most 50 MiB to more than 200 MiB after discovery, that comparison is false and runExhausted remains false despite a partial read. The run can consequently omit B6 and classify or admit a partial extract while the report claims exact coverage.
findings.recommendation: Depend on or include a reader fix that detects unread bytes from the current file-descriptor state rather than the stale discovery size, with an integration test for growth past the 200 MiB allowance. Until then, do not claim B6 is an exact production count.

machinery_findings.title: Acceptance criterion 5 can prove read-deferred disjointness only with an unreachable mocked state
machinery_findings.body: The two-run rewrite resolves the mutual exclusion between capacity and deadline stops, but both runs require readDeferred to be non-zero. Under the current 50 MiB discovery ceiling, fresh 200 MiB budget, and stale-size exhaustion check, a real dream collection cannot produce that state correctly. A test can satisfy the criterion only by forcing parse.runExhausted, so it would prove the array partition against a fabricated parser result while missing the production loss described above.
machinery_findings.recommendation: After fixing the reader, exercise B6 through a real bounded-read fixture or deterministic budget seam that reaches streamLines. Do not satisfy this criterion by directly mocking parse.runExhausted.
